name: Villanelle
note: Two lines said four times each. The form is built so that a refrain arrives in a different sentence every time and therefore means something different every time — if your refrains mean the same thing in stanza six as in stanza one, the form did nothing.
ground: A nineteenth-century French invention retrofitted onto a much older pastoral song, which is to say it is not ancient and does not need to be treated as sacred. It is a machine for obsession.
ask: Has either refrain changed meaning by the last stanza?
